cmad.notes: No CMAD located. (a) No designated CMAD repository is configured for this run; a Zenodo search for a Juno CMAD returned only records of the unrelated JUNO neutrino experiment. (b) Juno's data archive page at PDS PPI (https://pds-ppi.igpp.ucla.edu/mission/Juno) and the SwRI Mission Juno site carry no CMAD. (c) Web search for 'Juno CMAD' and 'Juno Calibration and Measurement Algorithms Document' found only per-instrument PDS Software Interface Specifications (MAG, JADE, JEDI, JIRAM), which are not CMADs. A CMAD is expected under this procedure because the record has no StopDate (operational) and Juno is NASA-funded, so this is recorded as an expected-but-not-located gap. Context for the reviewer: Juno is a Planetary Science Division New Frontiers mission reviewed in the Planetary Mission Senior Review, while the CMAD is a Heliophysics senior-review deliverable, so its absence may be unremarkable; and Juno's status after its extension through September 2025 could not be confirmed from a primary source (NASA's mission page still labels it an active mission; NSSDC says end of mission was scheduled for September 2025). Current-team evidence came instead from the mission team page (https://www.missionjuno.swri.edu/the-team/). Proceeded with the remaining sources.

instrument_coverage.notes: The registry reverse lookup (registry.py, all authorities) finds one Instrument record for spase://SMWG/Observatory/Juno: the Ephemeris virtual instrument (InstrumentType Platform). None of Juno's ten science investigations has an Instrument record under this Observatory. Roster from NASA's Juno mission page (ten instruments, including the Stellar Reference Unit), the mission team page's 'Investigation Payload' leads, the SwRI spacecraft page, NSSDC's experiment list (nine experiments; its JIRAM entry fails to load), and the chapters of the Springer 'The Juno Mission' volume (one paper per investigation). Short names used throughout: MAG (Magnetic Field Investigation: fluxgate magnetometers FGM plus Advanced Stellar Compass ASC), MWR, GRAV (Gravity Science: X-band transponder plus the Italian Ka-band translator KaT), JADE, JEDI, Waves, UVS, JIRAM, JunoCam, SRU (Stellar Reference Unit, used for the Radiation Monitoring Investigation, called RMI by NSSDC and RM in its paper). Roster conflicts with the record's own Description: it lists FGM and ASC as separate instruments (they make up MAG); it lists a Scalar Helium Magnetometer (SHM), which no other source names — the NSSDC description it was copied from has the same entry, so SHM looks like an error; it omits SRU/Radiation Monitoring; and it says both 'eight experiments' and 'ten instruments' while listing eleven items. Separately, CNES/CDPP-AMDA holds Instrument records for FGM, JADE, JEDI and WAVES (plus Ephemeris and magnetic-field Models) under its own Observatory record spase://CNES/Observatory/CDPP-AMDA/Juno; they do not point to the SMWG Juno Observatory, so they do not count here. Their PI Contacts were used as corroborating evidence.

notes: Paper selection (mission overview): confident. 'The Juno Mission' (Bolton et al. 2017, 10.1007/s11214-017-0429-6) has 18 authors, has 'Mission' in its title and names the observatory, is the most-cited Juno overview (Crossref 310, OpenAlex 361), and is the reference NSSDC lists for Juno. Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar agree on it and on its author order. SciX/ADS was not queried (no API token available), and Semantic Scholar answered only after repeated rate-limit waits. Timing: published November 2017, about six years after the 2011-08-05 launch that starts the OperatingSpan. That is a little outside the usual 2-5 year window, but Juno spent five years cruising to Jupiter and the paper came out about 16 months after Jupiter orbit insertion (July 2016), as the opening paper of the topical collection. This was not treated as a reason to downgrade. Candidates considered and rejected: Bolton & the Juno Science Team 2010 (IAU proceedings, 10.1017/s1743921310007313; only two bylines, one of them a team), Stephens 2015 (single-author operations paper) and Bagenal et al. 2017 (science objectives, not a mission description).

Alphabetization check (backward scan from the last author) on the mission overview paper: the longest sorted run at the end is three names (Mokashi, Thorne, Thorpe), so the list is not alphabetized. Positions 1-3 (Bolton, Lunine, Stevenson) were taken as Strong and positions 4-5 (Connerney, Levin) as Medium; positions 6-18 carry no position evidence.

Instrument papers: each one in the Space Science Reviews Juno topical collection (vol. 213, 2017) names its instrument in the title, has 7-50 authors, appeared online in 2013-2017 (before or soon after orbit insertion), and is the reference NSSDC gives for that experiment. Selection was confident for all ten. They are cited by their 2017 volume year, although several appeared online in 2013-2014.

Instrument-paper author orders. Not alphabetized (first three Strong, fourth and fifth Medium on the instrument's own record): Waves, UVS, JIRAM, JunoCam. JEDI: the first four authors precede an alphabetized remainder of sixteen (Mauk, Haggerty, Jaskulek Strong; Schlemm fourth). MAG: one lead author (Connerney), then fifteen in alphabetical order. JADE: the strict backward scan stops at the last name because White is appended after the two Wilsons, but positions 2-30 are otherwise alphabetical (apart from De Los Santos after Desai). Because a near-sorted list should not be read as contribution order, it was treated as one lead author (McComas) followed by an alphabetized remainder, so Alexander and Allegrini in positions 2-3 get no position weight. MWR: a six-name sorted run at positions 45-50 makes the list technically partly alphabetized, with the first 44 names as the deliberate prefix; positions 1-5 (Janssen, Oswald, Brown, Gulkis, Levin) were used. Gravity Science: fully alphabetized (Asmar to Simone), so no position weight at all. Radiation Monitoring (SRU): the team name 'The Selex Galileo Juno SRU Team' heads the byline and is not a person. It was counted as position 1, which keeps the position weight conservative: Becker and J. W. Alexander are Strong, and Adriani and Mura are recorded at positions 4-5.

Observatory scoping: for each instrument paper only positions 1-3 were included. Positions 4-5 are excluded as instrument-team depth and carry a Medium instrument_roles entry. Instrument-paper authors at position 4 or later who are included here (Gulkis, Levin, Ravine, Bagenal, Adriani on SRU, Mura on SRU) qualify through separate mission-level evidence: the mission overview paper, the team page's Co-Investigator list, or a named mission or instrument lead role.

Most of the included list comes from the Juno mission team page (https://www.missionjuno.swri.edu/the-team/). Its 'Co-Investigators' list names 55 people with an explicit Co-Investigator role, and each was included at Medium as CoInvestigator with observatory scope. Eight of them are marked deceased there (Anderson, Coradini, DeJong, Gautier, Klein, Owen, Smith, Thorne) and are kept, with the CoInvestigator source saying so. A curator should decide whether the full Co-Investigator roster belongs on the Observatory DOI or only its leads.

Instrument leads changed over the mission. Each earlier lead is recorded as FormerPI and the lead named on the current mission team page as InstrumentLead. JADE: David McComas (launch-era SwRI page; CDPP-AMDA JADE record), then Philip Valek (NSSDC PI), now Frédéric Allegrini. MWR: Michael Janssen (SwRI page; NSSDC), now Steve Levin. UVS: Randy Gladstone (SwRI page; NSSDC), now Thomas Greathouse. JIRAM: Alberto Adriani (INAF Media 2012/2016; Europlanet), now Alessandro Mura, earlier his deputy. Gravity Science: John Anderson (launch-era SwRI page; deceased), then William Folkner (NSSDC PI), now Ryan Park and Luciano Iess as co-leads. JunoCam has two current leads (Candice Hansen, Michael Ravine), and Gravity Science has two (Park, Iess). Unchanged leads: MAG (Connerney), JEDI (Mauk), Waves (Kurth), SRU (Becker). Mission PI Scott Bolton is the same in every source.

Program Scientist changed over time. NSSDC and this record's Contacts list Mary M. Mellott (Contacts give her role as ProjectScientist; NSSDC gives Program Scientist). The 2016 Jupiter orbit insertion press kit names Jared Espley, and NASA's program-officer page now names Delia L. Santiago-Materese. All three are recorded as ProgramScientist. Mellott's ProjectScientist Contact role conflicts with the team page and the press kit, which both name Steve Levin as Project Scientist, so the Observatory record's Mellott Contact should be corrected.

The Juno Ephemeris Instrument record (spase://SMWG/Instrument/Juno/Ephemeris) is a virtual Platform instrument. Its Contacts list only Mellott (ProjectScientist) and Bargatze (MetadataContact); neither is an instrument-level role, so it gets no instrument_roles entries and no pending run.
RevisionHistory names metadata editors only by initials (ZCB, JWL). These are metadata submissions, not authorship, and the initials do not identify anyone.

ORCIDs: only Connerney and Janssen have ORCIDs deposited in Crossref for these papers. All other ORCIDs come from OpenAlex's records for the cited Juno paper, where OpenAlex attaches ORCIDs algorithmically, so the enricher should validate each one. Affiliations come from the mission team page (for Co-Investigators) or the paper byline, with abbreviations expanded.

Bagenal et al. 2017 (Magnetospheric Science Objectives, 10.1007/s11214-014-0036-8) has one lead author (Bagenal) followed by 20 names in alphabetical order. It is a mission-level science paper, not the mission description paper, so its authors were used only as context.

Mission status: the record has no StopDate. NASA's mission page labels Juno an active mission, the SwRI site says 'Now in its extended mission', and NSSDC says end of mission was scheduled for September 2025. No primary source in this run confirms that operations continued or ended after September 2025, so the OperatingSpan stop may need a curator.

Mission-team-page and press-kit staff with engineering or management roles (project managers, engineers, mission managers, NASA Headquarters officials) are listed as excluded for having non-qualifying roles, so the reviewer can see they were considered.
